Welcome to Parklands
Welcome to Parklands Community Primary School.
I am delighted to be the Headteacher of this lovely community school. We are a friendly and busy school with a warm and welcoming ethos, which is recognised by all who visit. The Staff, Parents and Governors of our school all work together to provide the best for the families we serve. We want our children to enjoy their time and education with us and to achieve the highest possible standards in all aspects of their lives.
I hope you find the information on the website useful, please feel free to contact the office if you have any questions.

pageCache.text:
MFL - French
At Parklands Community Primary School we are communicators and linguists!
At Parklands Community Primary School, we are communicators and linguists! Our French curriculum is creative, practical, and full of fun, helping children build confidence to experiment with language—from saying “Bonjour” to holding conversations in Year 6. Through exciting, real-life scenarios and cross-curricular links, pupils gain a deeper understanding of different cultures while developing curiosity and independence in communication. Learning a language gives children a fresh perspective on their own identity and opens doors to a diverse, multicultural world. At Parklands, we spark a passion for language and global connection that lasts a lifetime!

pageCache.pageTitle: Parklands Community Primary School - Absence Procedures
pageCache.text:
Absence Procedures
School attendance is extremely important.
This year our attendance target is 97%. Please support us to achieve our target by only keeping children off school when absolutely necessary.
We ask, as much as possible, medical appointments are made outside of school hours. If your child has an appointment during school hours please notify the school office, in advance, with proof of the appointment, screen shots of the appointment text are acceptable.
If your child is absent due to illness please notify the office in one of the following ways:
Call: 01243 788630 option 1
Email: absent@parklands.school
To find out more information, please read our Attendance policy.
Absence Procedures

pageCache.pageTitle: Parklands Community Primary School - Our Specialist Support Centre
pageCache.text:
Our Specialist Support Centre
Parklands benefits from the inclusion of a Special Support Centre (Orchard Class and Forest Class).
There are 18 planned places for pupils with an Education Health and Care Plan (EHCP) specifying social communication needs. All pupils receive small group support from experienced teachers and special support assistants. The timetable offers a structured, academic curriculum that is teacher-led. Both classes follow the National Curriculum.
The West Sussex County Council guidance for SSC’s in mainstream schools asserts that;
“The overall aim of the provision is to support each pupil’s development academically, socially and emotionally through exposure to life in mainstream classes and individual or small group support from Special Support Centre Staff, in order to maximise inclusion.”
All pupils access elements of mainstream school life including assemblies, playtimes, clubs and lessons in their mainstream classes. A variety of strategies are employed to support effective inclusion for each pupil including personal learning plans, social skills lessons, speech and language therapy, Lego therapy, jump ahead physical education and the consistent use of visual timetables and social stories.
As the SSC is a Local Authority (LA)additionally resourced base, admission to the SSC is through the LA and children come from a wide geographical area.
For admissions details please click here.
Our Specialist Support Centre

pageCache.pageTitle: Parklands Community Primary School - Religious Education
pageCache.text:
Religious Education
At Parklands Community Primary School we are theologists!
At Parklands Community Primary School, we are theologists with curious minds! Our R.E. curriculum helps children explore big questions about beliefs, values, and the world around them. Through enquiry-based learning, pupils investigate major world religions, reflect on their own ideas, and develop respect and understanding for others. Lessons are creative, thought-provoking, and rooted in real-life experiences, encouraging discussion, critical thinking, and mindfulness. By the time they leave Parklands, our pupils are confident, tolerant, and inquisitive learners who celebrate diversity and are prepared for life in modern Britain.

pageCache.pageTitle: Parklands Community Primary School - Young Carers at Parklands
pageCache.text:
Young Carers at Parklands
At Parklands we recognise that some of our children are caring for a family member at home which may take up a little more of their time and this can be hard work. And although lots of young carers manage just fine, it’s still important they take care of themselves too. They deserve to be looked after, and we want to be able to offer these young people a supportive, fun environment where they can come and be themselves.
Parklands is working alongside West Sussex Young Carers to ensure our young people get the best and the right support as well as access to other events that are put on locally. This page will give details of events and support that will be on offer for our Young Carers. If you would like to talk to someone at West Sussex please call 01903 270300 or email youngcarers@westsussex.gov.uk.
If you think your young person is a carer, please get in touch with Mrs Earnshaw, Deputy Headteacher and Young Carer Lead at Parklands for an informal chat at office@parklands.school or on 01243 788630.
Young Carers at Parklands

pageCache.text:
Congratulations Parklands
Parklands has been awarded the 🎵Music Mark🎵 of Recognition for 'Ambition and Quality' by West Sussex Music. Well done Parklands!
News & Events
Latest News

Music
At Parklands Community Primary School we are musicians!
At Parklands Community Primary School, we are musicians who love to make noise! Our music curriculum is all about creativity, confidence, and joy. Every child gets the chance to sing, play instruments, and explore rhythms, melodies, and sounds. Through composing, performing, and even improvising, pupils develop teamwork, self-expression, and a lifelong love of music. From weekly assemblies and specialist lessons to exciting projects and community performances, music is woven into school life. By the time they leave Parklands, our pupils are confident performers with a strong understanding of musical language and an appreciation for a wide range of styles—because at Parklands, music is for everyone!

pageCache.pageTitle: Parklands Community Primary School - Our Governors
pageCache.text:
Our Governors
Parklands Community Primary School has a governing body made up of 12 committed and passionate volunteers, that play an important part in making our school the best it can be for its children, parents/carers and our staff.
The role of the Governing body is to provide strategic leadership of the school work in partnership with the Headteacher and have a vital role to play in ensuring every child gets the best possible education.
We do this by focusing on three core strategic functions:
The membership of the Governing Body is, as determined by law, made up of different types of governors. The Governing Body is made up of Parent Governors, Co-Opted Governors, a Local Authority Governor, a Staff Governor and the Headteacher.
Co-opted Governors (Elected by standing members of the governing body)
Mr D Barty
I first became a parent governor when our children joined Kingsham Primary School in reception class... They are now 36 and 34 respectively, so I have been involved with school governance for a few years... During that time, I have worked with many of the schools in our area and I have been both Chair and Vice-Chair of some of them.
As a (nearly) retired Finance Director for a local group of companies, my specialism has always been towards school finances, funding and resources. I have, however, been involved professionally in human resources, payroll, pensions, general administration and, on occasions, legal issues and I believe that I have a great deal to offer.
My wife (of 43 years) and I have lived in Chichester since moving here to start our own small business 46 years ago. Our children were both born, raised, and went to school in Chichester, and subsequently went on to Universities not too far from home and remain successful in their respective careers.
I am a strong believer that "every child matters" and this applies right across the very wide range of abilities that our dedicated teaching staff nurture each year. I therefore have no qualms in offering my voluntary support to the whole school community as a co-opted governor at your school.
Mr T Droar
Tony has built a distinguished career spanning education, technology, and public service, combining analytical expertise with a strong commitment to learning and community development. A graduate of the University of Bristol with a degree in Theoretical Physics, he has held leadership and project management roles in major organisations including IBM, ICL/Fujitsu, and West Sussex County Council, as well as in further and higher education institutions.
Tony also works part-time with the University of Portsmouth as a Project Supervisor, supporting students in developing their professional and research skills.
Other Activities and Community Involvement
ICL/Fujitsu – Project management and consultancy roles
Mrs B Drummond
Information to follow
Mrs J Foakes
I am a retired Tax Inspector, having spent most of my career with HMRC. After retirement, we moved to Chichester, 4 years ago, having spent 36 years in Reading, where we brought up our children. I am married to Martin and we have two adult children. I first got to know some of the children and staff of Parklands school through the church and was really pleased to be offered the opportunity to become one of your Governors. When I'm not at St Wilfrids, I volunteer at the Cathedral and for the Hospice. I play the clarinet in a band, and we like to spend time with our children and grandchildren.
Ms N Hiscock (Vice Chair of Governors)
I am local to the area and became a co-opted governor in 2022, following my son’s time at the school’s Specialist Support Centre (SSC). I currently serve as the SEND Link Governor and Chair of the Curriculum and Staffing Committee. My family’s experience of the SSC, and the wider processes involved in navigating the landscape of SEND support, has given me valuable insight into provision from both a parental and governance perspective.
I am incredibly passionate about the SEND system, particularly given the current pressures it faces, and I am committed to ensuring that all children in the school receive the support they need to thrive. Alongside my governor role, I sit on the SEND AP Board and the Steering Group for the West Sussex Parent Carer Forum (WSCPF), enabling me to contribute to, and influence, wider strategic discussions around SEND provision.
Outside of my governor role, I am also a local business owner, bringing practical experience and a strong understanding of accountability, leadership, and strategic decision-making to the governing body.
Local Authority Governor (Selected by the Local Authority (WSCC)
Mr D Millican (Chair of Governors and Link Governor)
David has been a governor of many different types of schools over a long number of years and is now proud to chair the governors of Parklands.
West Sussex County Council have appointed David onto their panel of Experienced Governors and he provides guidance to schools experiencing challenges.
David lives nearby and is active at Chichester Cathedral where he volunteers as a guide and with the education and creative learning team.
Headteacher Governor
Miss C Angeli
I’m proud to be the Headteacher of Parklands Community Primary School, supporting inclusive learning for all with over 10 years of experience in school leadership. I joined Parklands in 2023 after relocating from North London, and I’m really enjoying being closer to my family in West Sussex and discovering all that this beautiful part of the country has to offer. I’m passionate about giving children the best possible start in their primary years and love bringing warmth and positivity to school life. I enjoy singing, music, and swimming—and I always like to share a smile!
Parent Governors (Elected by current parents of the pupils of the school)
Ms J Best
Information to follow
Mrs J Hall
My name is Jo, and I am proud to serve as Parent Governor at Parklands since 2024. I live in Chichester with my husband and two lovely boys, both current Parklands pupils. I have lived in the Chichester area for over 11 years, moving back to be near where I grew up in West Sussex after finishing University to work as a doctor. I have an interest in the wellbeing of both staff and pupils, and I look forward to continuing to work alongside fellow Governors and staff to help support every child at Parklands to ‘Be the best you can be’.
Mrs M Kellermann
As a mum of two, with one child currently at Parklands, I’m passionate about creating a safe, inclusive environment where every child can thrive. I became a parent governor in late 2025 and look forward to working closely with the governors, staff and families. My background in Finance and Audit helps me support strong governance and resource oversight, and I’m committed to making decisions that put pupils first.
Mrs M Earnshaw
I have been really fortunate to have been working in education for 20 years and locally for most of that time in lots of different roles within teaching, including senior leadership. In January 2024, I was even more lucky to have been appointed Deputy Headteacher at Parklands! I love my job - I see it as a privilege to work alongside young people and helping them be the best they can be!
I love spending time with my two teenage boys, I love to sing and being by the sea.
Staff Governor (Elected by members of staff)
Mrs S Fancourt
I'm Selina Fancourt and I was elected as staff governor 2 years ago. I have worked at Parklands school for about 16 years and have enjoyed every minute. I have worked across every year group over the years.
I have a special interest in SEND and have my own autistic son. My daughter also went through Parklands and grew with confidence as she did.
I became a governor to help the school carry on in the future being the caring , family friendly school we have all grown to love.
For further information regarding our Governing Body, please contact: clerk@parklands.school

Science
At Parklands Community Primary School we are scientists!
At Parklands Community Primary School, we are scientists who love to explore! Our Science curriculum sparks curiosity and helps children understand the world through hands-on investigations and enquiry-based learning. Pupils learn to question, experiment, and reason scientifically while building knowledge of living things, materials, and physical processes. With practical activities, key vocabulary, and real-life contexts, science becomes exciting and meaningful. By the time they leave Parklands, our pupils are confident investigators who can think critically, work collaboratively, and explain their ideas—ready to discover the wonders of the world!
